title: The Five Pillars of Data Observability

scenes.title: The Five Pillars of Data Observability
scenes.subtitle: Freshness, volume, schema, distribution, lineage
scenes.narration: The five pillars give a shared vocabulary for describing every dimension of data health that observability should cover.

scenes.heading: The five pillars
bullets: Freshness: how recently the data was updated
Volume: how much data arrived versus expected
Schema: how the structure of the data changed
Distribution: whether values stay within expected ranges
Lineage: how tables and columns depend on one another
scenes.narration: Freshness tells you whether data is current, and volume tells you whether the expected amount actually arrived. Schema captures structural changes to columns and types, while distribution watches the statistical shape of the values themselves. Lineage ties it all together by mapping how upstream and downstream assets connect.

scenes.heading: How the pillars work together
steps: Freshness and volume catch pipeline delivery failures
Schema and distribution catch content-level problems
Lineage explains blast radius and root cause
scenes.narration: Freshness and volume are the first line of defense, catching pipelines that ran late or moved the wrong amount of data. Schema and distribution look inside the payload to catch structural and value-level defects. Lineage then connects an incident to its upstream cause and its downstream victims.

scenes.heading: Encoding pillars as monitors
scenes.code:
# Soda checks covering four pillars
checks for orders:
  # Freshness
  - freshness(created_at) < 6h
  # Volume
  - row_count between 900 and 1100
  # Schema
  - schema:
      fail:
        when required column missing: [order_id, amount]
  # Distribution
  - avg(amount) between 20 and 200
scenes.narration: This Soda configuration expresses four of the five pillars as declarative checks on the orders table. The freshness check fails if the newest record is older than six hours, and the volume check bounds the expected row count. The schema check guards required columns, while the distribution check keeps the average amount within a sane range.

scenes.text: Cover all five pillars and you catch late data, missing data, broken structure, drifting values, and their root cause.
scenes.narration: Each pillar closes a different gap, so a mature observability program monitors all five. Lineage is what turns detection into fast, confident diagnosis.
